title: Controllers in ASP.NET Core
description: Understand the role of controllers, how they process requests, and how data moves between views and controllers.

data.text: A **controller** is a C# class that receives incoming HTTP requests, processes them, and decides what response to send back. In the MVC pattern, the controller is the coordinator — it talks to the model (data), picks a view (UI), and sends the result to the browser.

terms.definition: A C# class that handles incoming requests, runs application logic, and returns a response.
A public method on a controller that handles a specific request.
A C# class that represents the data your application works with.
A Razor template (.cshtml) that generates the HTML sent to the browser.
The process of automatically mapping incoming form data to action method parameters or model properties.

data.caption: The MVC request pipeline: from browser request to rendered HTML response.
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A[Browser Request] --> B[Routing]
    B --> C[Controller]
    C --> D[Action Method]
    D --> E[Model / Data]
    E --> F[View]
    F --> G[HTML Response]
    G --> A

data.text: Controllers live in the `Controllers` folder. Every controller class name ends with `Controller` (for example, `HomeController`, `ProductController`). The class inherits from the `Controller` base class, which provides helper methods like `View()`, `RedirectToAction()`, and `Json()`.

data.content: The default controller created with a new ASP.NET Core MVC project.

data.title: Naming Convention
data.text: By convention, the `HomeController` class maps to URLs starting with `/Home`. The `Index` action maps to `/Home/Index`. ASP.NET Core routing handles this automatically.

Every controller has a matching folder inside `Views`. For example, `HomeController` has its views in `Views/Home/`. Each action typically has a view file with the same name — the `Index` action renders `Views/Home/Index.cshtml`.

Model Binding: Sending Data from Views to Controllers
Model Binding is the feature that automatically maps incoming form data to your action parameters or model class properties. You do not need to manually read `Request.Form` for each field.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Controllers receive HTTP requests and return responses via action methods.
Views live in the Views folder, organized by controller name.
ViewData and ViewBag pass small amounts of data; TempData survives one redirect.
Model Binding automatically maps form data to model classes.
File uploads use IFormFile with multipart/form-data forms.
data.takeaway: Controllers are the orchestrators of your ASP.NET Core app. Understanding how they talk to views and models is the foundation of everything else in MVC.
